title: Vukub-Cakix and the Hero Twins
subtitle: Pride, a fruit tree, and a blowpipe

pride.excerpt: In his own opinion Vukub-Cakix's existence rendered unnecessary that of the sun and the moon, and this egoism so disgusted the gods that they resolved upon his overthrow.

attack.excerpt: The hero-gods, who lay concealed within the foliage, now added injury to theft by hurling at Vukub-Cakix a dart from a blow-pipe, which had the effect of precipitating him from the summit of the tree to the earth. He arose in great wrath, bleeding profusely from a severe wound in the jaw.

narrativeBlocks.title: The boast that calls for a hero
narrativeBlocks.body: Vukub-Cakix is a giant bird-monster of the Popol Vuh who claims to be the sun and the moon — the world's most dangerous boast: taking the powers' place.

narrativeBlocks.title: The twins' answer
narrativeBlocks.body: The Hero Twins — Hunahpu and Xbalanque — take up their blowguns and climb into his tree, waiting for the boaster to come feed.

narrativeBlocks.title: The shot that breaks his jaw
narrativeBlocks.body: They shoot Vukub-Cakix in the jaw; he tears Hunahpu's arm off in the fight — and the battle that follows is a comedy of healing and counter-trickery.

narrativeBlocks.title: Teeth, medicine, and a fall
narrativeBlocks.body: The twins send two 'healers' — actually the twins disguised as grandparents — who pull his jade teeth and replace them with grains of corn; his pride literally goes to pieces.

narrativeBlocks.title: The pattern of the book
narrativeBlocks.body: The Vukub-Cakix episode is the Popol Vuh's rehearsal: the twins' true test is yet to come in Xibalba — this is the warmup, and the trickery is the signature.
